autonomy.definition: How much pg_sage may do on its own for one kind of Change on one database: ask first, act then tell you, or act in the maintenance window.

binding-fact.definition: A Fact a person confirmed that pg_sage must respect, for example that an index belongs to the application.

canary.definition: A first run of a Change on one database or a small part of the fleet, checked before it runs anywhere else.

change.definition: One thing pg_sage proposes to do to a database, such as creating an index, with its SQL, its risk and how it is undone.

custodian.definition: The person or team who owns a database and is told about its Issues.

decision.definition: A choice about a Change, always with who made it: a person (approve or reject), the policy (allow or hold back) or an agent, recorded with its reason.

fast-elevation.definition: Settings that let pg_sage earn Autonomy in hours instead of weeks; meant for test systems, and high-risk Changes still wait on you.

grandfathered.definition: Allowed because it was in place before a rule was added; new ones must follow the rule.

held-back.definition: A Change the policy did not let run, shown with the reason and what would let it run.

incident.definition: An Issue that is hurting the database now, such as an outage or a pile-up of locks.

investigation.definition: The work pg_sage does to explain an Issue: collecting evidence, testing ideas and saying what is still unknown.

issue.definition: Something on a database that needs attention, with the evidence pg_sage gathered for it and what is still unknown.

lifecycle.definition: Where an Issue or a Change stands: open, in progress, resolved, rolled back or dismissed.

minimum-evidence.definition: The verified outcomes pg_sage needs before it may propose more Autonomy for a kind of Change.

observation-mode.definition: pg_sage watches the database and proposes Changes, but changes nothing on it.

plan.definition: An ordered set of Changes pg_sage proposes together for one Issue, with a check after each step; you decide on the whole Plan or on each step.

policy-check.definition: The rules every Change passes before it runs: its risk, the maintenance window, its reach and the Autonomy you gave.

risk-tier.definition: How much harm a Change could do if it went wrong: safe, moderate or high; a high-risk Change always waits on you.

shadow-decision.definition: What pg_sage would have done with more Autonomy, recorded without acting so it can be compared with what a person decided.

source-fix.definition: A Change to the application or to the query text rather than the database; pg_sage can suggest it but cannot apply it.

specialist.definition: A narrow agent inside pg_sage for one kind of work, such as vacuum or indexes, with a written limit on what it may propose.

verification.definition: The check after a Change runs that it did what was expected; when it did not, pg_sage rolls the Change back.

waiting-on-you.definition: Changes and Plans that need a person's Decision before they can run.

what-if-check.definition: A test of an index that does not exist yet (with HypoPG) to see whether a query would use it, without building it.
